title: Big spike: 2 replicas are not enough
story: 100 users against one 0.5 CPU replica. Two replicas still saturate; three hold. Expected: resolved, possibly via rollback and a second attempt.

args.summary: Scaled shop from 1 to 3 replicas to relieve CPU-bound request queuing (peak CPU 53% vs 50% per-replica limit) causing 1800ms latencies and client timeouts/broken pipes; allowed_actions permits scale only and service is stateless.

args.reason: Scaling shop from 1→3 replicas did not resolve the incident: all 3 replicas are healthy with low memory (21.5MB/128MB) and modest CPU (54% total across 3 replicas, i.e. ~18%/replica, well under the 50% per-replica limit), yet probe latency remains pinned at exactly 1800ms on 5/5 consecutive checks post-scale. The uniform, unchanging 1800ms latency regardless of replica count or CPU headroom (versus the pre-incident flat 22ms) indicates a fixed artificial delay/config issue in the app (e.g. SHOP_WORK_MS env var or MODE flag) rather than CPU-bound queuing — logs also show BrokenPipeError from clients giving up on that fixed-length response, not resource contention. This is a code/config root cause outside the 'scale' guardrail's reach; WatchDock will auto-rollback the ineffective replica change. Needs a human to inspect/adjust SHOP_MODE/SHOP_WORK_MS env vars or app code at app/svc.py:66.

result.error: a fix is already applied; WatchDock will verify it and roll back if it fails

timeline.thought:
ROOT CAUSE: Not CPU saturation — probe latency jumped from a flat ~22ms to a uniform, unvarying 1800ms on every request (p50=max=1800ms, 3 consecutive timeouts) while memory stayed low (21.4MB/128MB, no OOM) and CPU was moderate (avg 13%, peak 53% on a 50%-limit replica). Logs show BrokenPipeError when the server tries to write a response the client already gave up on — consistent with a fixed, artificial per-request delay (likely driven by the SHOP_WORK_MS/SHOP_MODE env vars) rather than queuing from load.

CHANGE: Applied a scale-out from 1→3 replicas (the only allowed_action) as the first hypothesis, since peak CPU (53%) was at/above the per-replica 50% limit, suggesting possible contention.

GUARDRAILS: Within limits (replicas 3 ≤ max_replicas 3); dry-run passed with no violations. Verification after apply showed the fix did not work: post-scale status still shows 5/5 probes at exactly 1800ms with CPU now only ~18%/replica (54% total / 3) and stable low memory — confirming latency is independent of replica count/CPU headroom, so WatchDock will auto-rollback this ineffective change.

FOLLOW-UP: This is a config/code issue outside the 'scale' guardrail's reach. A human should inspect app/svc.py (around line 66, do_GET) and the SHOP_MODE/SHOP_WORK_MS environment variables for a fixed/injected delay or bug introduced near incident time, since no resource change can fix a constant per-request delay unrelated to load or resources.

Memory is not the issue (21.5MB peak vs 128MB limit, no OOM kills). Per this service's guardrails, cpus and memory changes are not in allowed_actions, so we cannot raise the per-replica cpu limit to relieve the saturation, and we have already exhausted the only permitted lever (replica count) at its ceiling without success. Reapplying the same already-maxed, already-failed scale action is not expected to succeed and risks burning another heal cycle; this needs a human decision to either raise the cpus/max_replicas guardrail for shop or investigate the app for a periodic stall independent of load.

# s15

## Purpose
Shop front-end API on launch day.

## Hardware
Raspberry Pi 4: 4 CPUs, 4 GiB RAM shared by every service on the device.

## Notes for the agent
- Stateless HTTP API behind traefik. Horizontal scaling is safe; traefik picks up new replicas by label.
- Each request is CPU-bound (about 20 ms of CPU), so throughput per replica is set by its cpus limit.
- Never change image, ports, labels or environment.

## Incident ledger
| when (UTC) | trigger | evidence | action | result | commit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

args.reason: Root cause is CPU saturation per replica: with 1 replica CPU sits at 49% of the 0.5-cpu (50%) limit and probe latency is pinned at 1800ms (5/5 recent probes), matching the "about 20ms CPU per request" note in watchdock.md once concurrent load exceeds what a single 0.5-cpu replica can drain. The only guardrail-permitted action for this service is "scale" (allowed_actions: [scale]), and attempt 1 already scaled shop from 1→3 replicas (the max_replicas ceiling). That change was applied and then auto-rolled back by WatchDock because the probe series continued to alternate between healthy (~22-94ms) and saturated (1200-1800ms) readings throughout the 60s verification window (e.g. t=39.6→1400ms, 45.6→1391ms, 57.5→1343ms, 67.6→1371ms, 73.5→1290ms, 81.5→1335ms, 85.6→1375ms) instead of settling for 5 consecutive good probes, i.e. 3 replicas (the max allowed) is still not enough headroom to clear the backlog, and/or there is a recurring per-replica stall unrelated to raw replica count. Memory is not the issue (21.5MB peak vs 128MB limit, no OOM kills). Per this service's guardrails, cpus and memory changes are not in allowed_actions, so we cannot raise the per-replica cpu limit to relieve the saturation, and we have already exhausted the only permitted lever (replica count) at its ceiling without success. Reapplying the same already-maxed, already-failed scale action is not expected to succeed and risks burning another heal cycle; this needs a human decision to either raise the cpus/max_replicas guardrail for shop or investigate the app for a periodic stall independent of load.
